comment: Every place a source is weaker than it looks, and every place this package deliberately claims nothing. The facts themselves live in hardware.json; this file is about their standing.

sources.cartridges: The driver routines inside the 42 cartridges cartridges.manifest.json names, 36 of them DSP cartridges, each identified by digest before a byte is read.
sources.document: Nintendo's Book II, for the DSP's two windows in Figures 3-1-4 and 3-1-5. Book I documents the memory map and not what a cartridge board decodes for a coprocessor, and no document covers the ST010, ST011, ST018 or OBC1.
sources.implementations: Emulators, which were written by people reading the same cartridge code this package reads. Not a separate source.

divergences.documentSays: For the DSP, Book II's Figures 3-1-4 and 3-1-5 print both windows, with the mirror banks. For every other part, nothing: no manufacturer document known gives the address lines a cartridge board decodes for it.
divergences.referenceDoes: Every driver read agrees with the window this package uses for its part and layout.
divergences.reasoning: Narrowed on 2026-10-19 by reading Book II. The DSP's windows are now documented, marked verified, and widened to the mirror banks the figures print, which the drivers alone never showed. For the other parts, agreement across independently written drivers is strong evidence and is not a document, and it still cannot say where a window stops, because a driver shows where a part answers and never where it does not.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A Seta or Nintendo document for the ST010, ST011, ST018 and OBC1, or a continuity reading across a real cartridge board.

divergences.reasoning: That agreement is worth nothing as corroboration, because those emulators were written by people reading the same cartridge code. Counting it as a second witness would be counting the same evidence twice, and this is written down so nobody does.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: Anything that did not come from reading a driver: a schematic, a board photograph, a continuity reading, or a manufacturer note.

divergences.referenceDoes: Nothing either, for a part no cartridge in the manifest carries.
divergences.reasoning: A window is only listed where a driver was actually read. A part with no cartridge present gets no entry rather than an entry copied from somewhere else, and a lookup for it raises instead of guessing.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A cartridge carrying that part, added to the manifest and read.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing about timing, and this package asks nothing about it.
divergences.reasoning: What one of these accesses costs the console belongs to snes-mapper-python, and how long the part runs afterwards belongs to snes-dsp-python. This package reads what a driver says, not how long it waits.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: n/a. This is a scope boundary rather than an unknown.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing. This is about what this package can claim.
divergences.referenceDoes: Nothing comparable: a reimplementation runs the code and never has to say where it thinks an access landed.
divergences.reasoning: A long load or store spells all three bytes of its address, so the bank is read. An ordinary absolute one spells two and takes the third from the data bank register, which nothing here tracks. Until the ST018 every part this package knew was reached long, so an absolute access read as no access at all. It now answers with the bank the routine executes in, and Step.banked and Conversation.banked are how a caller tells a read bank from an assumed one, because a shape that mixed the two silently would claim more than it knows. Measured on 2026-10-19 with conformance.executed: Hayazashi Nidan Morita Shougi 2 reaches the ST018 from three instructions in its first 2,000,000, and half of the addresses they reach carry data bank 2B while the routine runs in bank 00.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: Tracking the data bank register through a walk, which needs an entry state a walk starting at one routine does not have.

divergences.referenceDoes: nothing; this is about what this package can read, not about a part
divergences.reasoning: A walk now steps into a callee and comes back, and descends only into one it has first walked to a return. The condition is not caution for its own sake: a call whose destination is a jump table or a block of constants still disassembles, because every byte is some opcode, and an unconditional descent spent the budget there and never returned for the caller's own accesses. One F1-ROC II routine calls into a region that decodes as brk, and following it dropped the four accesses made afterwards: the longest ST010 exchange fell from six accesses to four. Made conditional, the same cartridge reads ten. What is left is a helper that reaches the part and exits through a computed jump, whose accesses are read as a routine of their own. Since 2026-10-19 both widths after a stepped-over call are unknown unless the sweep from the vectors arrived at the next instruction with exactly one pair; before, the walk assumed the call left them as it found them.
wouldSettleIt: running the image rather than reading it, which belongs to another member

divergences.reasoning: Any access landing in a status range used to become a poll whichever way it went, so a console writing a control register and a console reading it made the same entry. The ST018 reset pulse is three writes to $3804 and read as poll1 poll1 poll1. The range is now split by direction the way the data range already was, and every recorded shape that touches a status range was re-read from the cartridges rather than edited.

divergences.referenceDoes: nothing; this is about what this package can read, not about a part
divergences.reasoning: conversation.reached starts at every vector a low cartridge publishes and decodes only what control flow arrives at, which is how a part reached by an ordinary absolute access is found at all. jmp ($1234) and its two indexed relatives are not followed, so what comes back is the routines that were found rather than proof there are no others. Metal Combat is the measured case: seeding from reset alone reached 1,675 instructions and from all ten vectors 2,080; since the sweep carries both widths through every call and stops at an immediate whose width it does not know, 1,556 and 1,961 distinct instructions. Through banks 00 to 3F alone neither run reached the OBC1; through the mirror banks 80 to BF the cartridge also uses, the walk reaches it from 19 instructions, while a search for the bytes that spell a long access finds 313 sites. A part the sweep finds nothing for is unread rather than uncontacted. Narrowed on 2026-10-19: conformance.executed runs the image on the 65816 core, and Metal Combat (USA) run for 2,000,000 instructions from reset reaches the OBC1 from 147 distinct instructions, all absolute accesses from routines running in bank 80; the vector walk finds 19 of them and the byte search none. The run is a floor, against a console that answers every register but the blanking bits with 0.
wouldSettleIt: shapes read out of a run rather than a walk
a jump table whose bounds this could read

divergences.documentSays: Nothing. The accumulator's width at a routine's entry is set by whoever called it, and nothing in the routine says what it was.
divergences.referenceDoes: snes-st-python at commit 50c8414 records a headless MAME write tap on the ST010 cartridge: the command start is one 16-bit store of 80nnH to 680020H, the command byte and the start bit in one word write, made by the cartridge's own bytes at file offset 0x0D66. snes-obc1-python at commit 76fc227 records, with a headless MAME 0.289 run, Metal Combat writing 7FF4 as the high byte of a 16-bit store to 7FF3, from six instructions in bank 82, each after ora #$0200 or and #$FDFF.
divergences.reasoning: shapes walks every routine with an 8-bit accumulator at entry. F1-ROC II's start routine is entered 16-bit: read 8-bit, the bytes at 0x0D66, A9 06 80, decode as lda #$06 followed by a branch, the walk leaves the routine there and reports write1 write1; read 16-bit from the same entry, at reports write2 write2 write2 poll2 read2 read2, whose third store is the start word the tap recorded. The walk carries a width through sep and rep but cannot know the one it starts with, so every shape recorded from a routine entered wide is wrong in its widths and may be cut short. snes-st-python's st010shapes.json was taken that way. Narrowed on 2026-10-19: a walk now starts with the width unknown unless told, learns it from sep, rep and a plp matching a php it saw, records an access of unknown width as width None and shape token ?, and ends at an accumulator immediate whose length it cannot know. It no longer reports a width it did not read; it still cannot report one it was not shown. Narrowed again on 2026-10-19: told the layout, shapes starts each walk at the widths the sweep from the vectors arrived with. The sweep tracks the accumulator and the index registers, enters every callee once per pair of widths its callers leave, resumes each caller at every pair the callee returns with, and leaves both unknown after a call through a table, out of the image, or into a callee it never sees return. A routine entered at two widths gives a shape for each, and a width a run of the image used settles an entry the sweep left unknown, marked *. Measured on 2026-10-19 across the 42 cartridges on hand: the sweep arrives with a known accumulator width at 221 of 7,398 sites and at none with two; 57 of the 5,160 exchanges shapes reads carry no ?, among them an F1-ROC II routine at 0x3E1D read 16 bits wide whose second store is the word 8007 to 68:0020, the command-and-start form the MAME tap recorded from the routine at 0x0D66, which the sweep does not reach. A 2,000,000-instruction run settles none of the open sites. Metal Combat's word stores to 7FF3, whose bytes sit at 0x10135 and 0x10143 in bank 82, stay out of reach: the sweep decodes nothing in that bank and the run executes nothing there. Narrowed again on 2026-10-19 at the emulator rung: conformance.traced ran each of the 42 cartridges headless in MAME 0.289, 3,600 frames untouched and 7,200 with buttons pressed, and kept every access to the part's window whose instruction, decoded from the cartridge's own bytes under the recorded M and X flags, spells the address and moves the width the bus moved. 3,104 instructions passed and sit in conformance/traced.json; 2,727 groups of accesses did not and are kept as disagreements. shapes fills a ? from that corpus at the same instruction and marks it ~. 4,874 of the 5,160 exchanges still carry ?, against 5,103, and 6,549 of 7,853 accesses, against 6,945. The trace agrees with both earlier taps: the store at 0x0D69 and the stores at 0x10135 and 0x10143 each moved two bytes on every execution recorded. Six DSP cartridges never reached the part in either run.
wouldSettleIt: runs that reach gameplay in every cartridge, which needs input written for each game
a jump table whose bounds this could read
a logic analyser on a real cartridge's bus, for a width settled rather than traced
